correctness.rationale: The odd Sym^r representation has a nondegenerate alternating apolar form. Rank loss of moment-map differential is exactly existence of a nonzero annihilating Lie algebra element; semisimple elements have no zero weight and nilpotents annihilate only pure powers. In the exact three-quadric complete intersection, this classifies the entire reduced singular locus. In a slice the 2 pivots are 2a_{r-1},2a_r. The remaining weighted hypersurface has rank 2p-1 transverse Hessian, a one-dimensional kernel, and an equivariant critical value of weight r+1 forcing c*t^(p+2). If c=0, the singular set would contain a transverse curve, contradicting the rank-loss result, so c is nonzero. Morse splitting yields the normal form; exact differentiation gives local singular length p+1. Exact verifier replays quadratic ranks and low-degree coefficients.

value.rationale: This resolves a natural structural gap for an infinite family of integral complete intersections: the full geometric singular support, simple singularity type uniformly controlled by p, and exact nonreduced Jacobian multiplicity along the rational normal curve. Neither the scheme-theoretic multiplicity nor the transverse analytic exponent follows from degree/integrality alone. These invariants bear on singular-cycle, deformation and local-resolution calculations. The result is not merely a rephrasing of the original complete-intersection degree.
